To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the deficiency of the innate defense molecule surfactant protein-D (SP-D) is associated with impaired clearance of respiratory syncytiol virus (RSV), increased inflammation in the lung, and increased mortality after infection.
SP-D binds RSV and enhances phagocytic and microbicidal activity of alveolar macrophas and neutrophils.
SP-D enhances pulmonary clearance of RSV by binding to the RSV envelope glycoproteins and enhancing phagocytotic uptake by macrophages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of SP-D with RSV, and the role of SP-D in the host immune response to RSV infection.
the role of SP-D in innate host defense against RSV and other viral infections.
the mechanisms by which SP-D enhances the innate host defense against RSV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SP-D is involved in host defense mechanisms against RSV.
SP-D plays an important role in innate immunity to RSV infection by enhancing pulmonary clearance, decreasing inflammation, and increasing phagocytotic activity.
SP-D is a critical component of innate immunity to RSV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SP-D is an important host defense molecule against RSV.
SP-D is a key molecule in innate defense against respiratory viral infection.

SP-D is a novel innate defense protein that enhances pulmonary clearance of RSV and that deficiency in the SP-D gene is associated with impaired pulmonary clearance of R SV and increased pulmonary inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SP-D enhances pulmonary clearance of RSV, and this may contribute to the protection against RSV afforded by SP-D.
SP-D plays a role in innate immune responses to RSV and may be a useful target for therapeutic interventions.
SP-D is a key component of innate immunity to RSV infection.
